children: , a biopharmaceutical company leading a new era in the treatment of central nervous system (CNS) disorders, today announced presentations of new data in major depressive disorder and Alzheimer’s disease agitation and eight additional encore data posters spanning its psychiatry and neurology portfolio at Psych Congress 2026, being held September 15-19, in New Orleans, Louisiana.
Details of the data presentations are as follows:
Agitation in Alzheimer’s Disease: Association with Increased Clinical Burden, Healthcare Utilization, and Mortality Among Patients in Long-term Care
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Malcolm Fraser, MD, CMD, Medical Director, Red Rock Pharmacy, Salt Lake City, UT
Real-World Treatment Patterns and Clinical Management of Alzheimer’s Disease Agitation
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Amita Patel, MD, CMD, MHA, CPE, private practice, Dayton OH
Results of a Survey of Care Partners of People Living with Alzheimer’s Disease Agitation
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Brent P. Forester, MD, MSc; Professor, Department of Psychiatry, Tufts University School of Medicine, MA
Anti-Anhedonic Effects of Dextromethorphan-Bupropion Mediate Improvements in Functioning and Quality of Life in Major Depressive Disorder
Thursday, September 17, 9:00 - 10:00 a.m. at the “Latest Discoveries & Emerging Trends in MDD” session, and 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Andrew Cutler, MD, Clinical Associate Professor of Psychiatry, SUNY Upstate Medical University, NY
Real-World Clinical Outcomes of Patients Switching to Treatment with Dextromethorphan-Bupropion (45 mg/105 mg)
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Joel L. Young, MD, Medical Director of the Rochester Center for Behavioral Medicine, MI
Anxiolytic Effects of Dextromethorphan-Bupropion (45mg/105mg): Post Hoc Analyses Across Trials in Major Depressive Disorder
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Jeffrey R. Strawn, MD, Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neuroscience, University of Cincinnati, OH
Effects of Dextromethorphan-Bupropion (45mg/105mg) in Participants with Major Depressive Disorder and Anxious Distress
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Jeffrey R. Strawn, MD, Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Neuroscience, University of Cincinnati, OH
Excessive Daytime Sleepiness in Narcolepsy and OSA:
Solriamfetol for Excessive Daytime Sleepiness in Narcolepsy and OSA: Post-hoc Multi-dimensional Composite Endpoint Analysis of Phase 3 Trials
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Wermter, Ellen E., FNP-BC, DBSM, FAASM, Restorative Sleep Medicine, Charlottesville, VA
Cognitive and Functional Outcomes from the Phase 3 Open-Label Extension and Randomized-Withdrawal ENCORE Trial of AXS-12 in Narcolepsy with Cataplexy
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Bruce Corser MD, FAASM, Medical Director of Intrepid Research, Cincinnati, OH
Symptom Burden and Quality of Life in Patients with Narcolepsy Who Continue to Experience Cataplexy: Subgroup Analysis from the CRESCENDO Survey
Thursday, September 17, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m., and Friday, September 18, 12:00 - 3:30 p.m. Central Time
Michael J. Thorpy, MD, Director of the Sleep-Wake Disorders Center at the Montefiore Medical Center and Professor of Neurology at Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York, NY

Axsome Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company leading a new era in the treatment of central nervous system (CNS) conditions. We deliver scientific breakthroughs by identifying critical gaps in care and develop differentiated products with a focus on novel mechanisms of action that enable meaningful advancements in patient outcomes. Our industry-leading neuroscience portfolio includes FDA-approved treatments for major depressive disorder, agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease, excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy and obstructive sleep apnea, and migraine, as well as multiple novel product candidates addressing a broad range of serious neurological and psychiatric conditions that impact over 150 million people in the United States. Together, we are on a mission to solve some of the brain’s biggest problems so patients and their loved ones can flourish. For more information, please visit us at
